findings.evidence: A one-line fix, no body needed: `fix(auth): treat a token at its expiry time as expired`
findings.fix: The three worked messages are templates a user can ask for, so keep them in references/. Move the three lines that only restate Conventional Commits defaults the model already writes (one-line fix needs no body; the body says why; mark a break in the header and the footer) into the Message checklist as one rule, and record that shortening in docs/audit/recovery/commit-work/record.md.

findings.evidence: if `git apply --cached --check` fails, stop and ask, and never edit inside a hunk
findings.fix: Name the failure mode: a failed `--check` means the copied header or a deleted hunk boundary is wrong, and editing a line count or context line makes `git apply` accept a patch that no longer matches the file. Keep the stop-and-ask rule.

findings.evidence: Read `references/split-one-file.md` when one file holds hunks for two different commits
findings.fix: After that sentence add: Do NOT load `references/split-one-file.md` when the file is wholly approved, the hunks belong to one commit, or the file is untracked (ask for the approved content instead).

findings.evidence: The summary starts with a concrete verb (`fix`, `add`, `remove`, `rename`) rather than `Update` or `Change`.
findings.fix: Add the condition: this applies only when the repository has no subject-case rule. Under `@commitlint/config-conventional`, `subject-case` rejects a capitalised verb, so the summary stays lowercase (`fix(auth): treat a token at its expiry time as expired`).

findings.evidence: Shows ordered `git status`, `git diff`, `git add -- src/auth.ts`, `git diff --cached`, and `git commit` commands.
findings.fix: review-and-commit omits the scratch directory the workflow always creates. Assert a proposed `mktemp -d "$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/commit-work.XXXXXX"` and an `rm -rf -- "<run>"` of only that directory, and keep the existing ordered status, diff, add, cached-diff and commit assertions.

findings.evidence: When the user approved a path's staged diff, commit that exact staged version and never restage the whole working-tree file over it
findings.fix: Before the overlap check, add the case the approved path also has unstaged edits: `git add -- <path>` would replace the approved staged blob. Copy the staged blob with `git diff --cached --binary -- <path>` and `git apply --cached` into the temporary index (or leave it untouched in the real index) and do not `git add` that path.
